findings.finding: The overlap-switch threading inventory for run_pass1 is incomplete: the plan asserts review_plan threads the parameter 'to run_pass1 (pass1.py:232)', but review_plan does not call run_pass1. run_pass1's only src/ caller is ProductionBatchRunner.run at production_batch_runner.py:152, which builds run_pass1's arguments from a BatchRunRequest (req), not from a parameter passed down from review_plan. The intermediate patch sites required to actually carry a boolean from review_plan to run_pass1 are unnamed.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the >10-candidate retrieval (AC2/AC3) with ADR 0122's k=5 decision: either justify the operating-point change by re-running `evals/similar-tickets/measure.py --paired` at the new k and amending ADR 0122, or constrain overlap retrieval to k=5 so the shared tier's measured basis is preserved.
evidence: ADR 0122 Decision: 'k=5 is part of the decision, not an implementation detail. ... A future change to the surfaced count invalidates this ADR and must re-run --paired.'

ADR 0122: 'At k=10 vector's semantic advantage disappears into noise (p=0.3438) while fts5's lexical advantage becomes significant (p=0.0000) — at that operating point the evidence favours keeping fts5 and building nothing.'
src/rebar/similar/lexical.py:14-18: 'The result cap is 5, and that is part of the decision. ... Returning a different count would invalidate the comparison the ADR rests on.'
AC2 itself: 'RESULT_LIMIT is 5 ... so retrieval must raise limit above its default' — an explicit operating-point change.

Plan claims the embedding tier is a strength ('With the optional embedding tier configured it ranks through that tier'), yet ADR 0122 shows that tier has no distinguishable advantage at k=10, the very regime the plan creates.
findings.finding: The plan raises the retrieval surfaced count above k=5 (AC2 requires >10 candidates offered, AC3 injects 10) but does not reconcile this with ADR 0122, which declares k=5 a load-bearing architectural decision and requires re-running the paired benchmark on any change to the surfaced count.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria lines 2-3 ('Retrieval offers more than 10 candidates...'; 'At most 10 candidates are injected'); Approach §'Reuse the index'
scenarios: Overlap retrieval runs with the embedding tier configured and surfaces >10 candidates: operating in the k=10 regime where ADR 0122 shows the embedding tier buys nothing and lexical is distinguishably better.
A future reader trusts the shipped k>10 count as validated when ADR 0122's measurement covers only k=5.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach subsection addressing ADR 0122: state whether overlap retrieval operates at k=5 (preserving the measured operating point and the existing cap) or at a higher k, and if higher, make re-running `--paired` at that k and amending ADR 0122 an explicit deliverable with an AC.
